grh_4f572bcc6e2a6cd4fa67.title: The Damned Dont Cry
paragraphs: Ethel Whitehead escapes a life of poverty by remaking herself as the sophisticated Lorna Hansen Forbes, but every step upward draws her deeper into George Castleman's criminal organization. Ambition, luxury and divided loyalties cost her the people who once mattered to her, while her relationship with Castleman's rival Nick Prenta turns the underworld power struggle personal. After Nick is killed, Ethel finally turns against the racket and gives the full story to a newspaperman so other desperate women will understand the price of taking her path. Castleman comes for her in the final confrontation; Ethel is wounded, but his attempt to silence her is stopped and she is left to face what her ambition has cost.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Joan Crawford, [[person|frank-lovejoy|Frank Lovejoy]], Paul Frees, Eddie Fields, and Ken Christy. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Howard Wiley as producer, Jack Rubin as radio adaptor, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 60 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.0ee8343bca2245d4|Chesterfield]] and [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.940a4ebed3ed3581|The Damned Dont Cry]]. Jack Rubin adapted it for radio.

grh_4f0139e20f03a78e03de.title: Ben Scofield
paragraphs: A masked young robber steals a large sum and shoots a man during the escape, and Britt joins Sheriff Ed Scofield in following the trail. The tracks and the robber's age increasingly point toward Ed's own son Ben, who had recently lost money gambling, forcing the sheriff to continue the hunt even while insisting his boy could not have changed into a killer overnight. Britt corners the wounded fugitive at an isolated cabin and survives a shootout. When the prisoner is finally seen clearly, he is not Ben, confirming Ed's faith in his son.

grh_4f3c1d8ccaea62acf09c.title: Paris Is Not the Same
paragraphs: Harry returns to Paris and rekindles feelings for the wife of a mild-mannered man while joining a scheme that dilutes expensive perfume and resells the doctored bottles to unsuspecting buyers. When the operation begins to unravel, the husband learns enough about Harry's criminal involvement and offers him 50,000 francs to leave Paris permanently and sign a confession that can be turned over to police if he returns. Harry accepts but decides that merely leaving will not end the woman's attachment to him. After an accident leaves another man dead with his face crushed beyond recognition, Harry plants his own identification on the body and lets Paris believe Harry Lime is dead. Much later the grateful husband tells the very-much-alive Harry that the apparent death finally ended his wife's grief and restored their marriage.

The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Harry Lime]].

grh_4fb387c5033c2908658d.title: Murder Beyond the Mountains
paragraphs: During the years when the world believes him dead, Holmes travels as Sigerson to a Tibetan monastery where several foreigners seek permission from a Chinese envoy to continue to Lhasa. When the envoy is strangled after rejecting their requests, Russian cigarette ash seems to implicate Borodin, but Holmes notes that the killer used a left hand Borodin cannot use because his is artificial. The planted clue instead exposes the supposed American missionary as a German agent trying to reach Lhasa ahead of the Russians. paragraphs: Holmes and Watson infiltrate an exclusive society of beggars and discover that its leaders are anarchists exploiting mendicant disguises to move freely around London and prepare an attack during the coming Jubilee. grh_4f05ba49cefd48ab92df.title: Wartime Racketeers
paragraphs: A warning about home-front crime dramatizes the many ways racketeers exploit wartime shortages, regulations and grief. Episodes cover scalped train tickets, black-market food and gasoline, counterfeit ration coupons, fraudulent allotment marriages and impostors who demand money from families of servicemen. The broadcast argues that these schemes survive because ordinary citizens cooperate with them and urges the public to report fraud, obey rationing rules and deny criminals the customers they need.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
